title: Water Damage Mitigation Training Note: How the Carpet Came Up and the Treated Floor
content:
**Training note — Water Damage Mitigation antimicrobial treatment**

How the carpet came up sets the treated floor of a tear-out antimicrobial line: when the job carries pad removal lines and carpet detach-and-reset lines, the back of the lifted carpet is treated along with the floor, so the treated floor is the affected floor area plus the square feet on the carpet detach-and-reset lines; when it carries pad removal lines and carpet removal lines, the treated floor is the larger of the affected floor area and the square feet on the carpet removal lines, because the discarded carpet often runs past the mapped wet area; in any other case no carpet-based change to the treated floor applies.

## Questions answered
**What records decide it?** The job's own charge lines: whether it carries pad removal lines, carpet detach-and-reset lines and carpet removal lines, and the square feet on them; and the affected floor area on the job record.

**Carpet lifted and reset, pad replaced?** Pad removal plus carpet detach-and-reset: the treated floor is the affected floor area plus the detach-and-reset square feet.

**Carpet and pad both thrown out?** Pad removal plus carpet removal: the treated floor is whichever is larger, the affected floor area or the carpet removal square feet.

**Carpet removed but no pad removal line?** Neither combination is present, so no carpet-based change applies.

## Worked figures (hypothetical affected floor area of 640 square feet)
| Lines on the job | Treated floor |
|---|---|
| pad removal, carpet detach-and-reset of 300 sq ft | 940 square feet |
| pad removal, carpet removal of 710 sq ft | 710 square feet (larger than 640) |
| pad removal, carpet removal of 520 sq ft | 640 square feet (larger than 520) |
| flood cut lines only | no carpet-based change |
